evals.prompt: Our endpoint parses a small 2KB JSON string. Should we move serde_json::from_str to spawn_blocking to keep the async loop fast?
evals.expected_output: Recommends direct execution on the Tokio worker thread instead of spawn_blocking, pointing out that context switching and queue overhead exceed the short work duration.
assertions: Recommends direct execution on Tokio worker thread for short CPU work
Rejects spawn_blocking due to thread context switch overhead
References workload-driven execution matrix in tokio-performance

evals.prompt: We have a synchronous file read std::fs::read_to_string inside an async function. How should we handle this in Tokio?
evals.expected_output: Recommends using tokio::fs::read_to_string or tokio::task::spawn_blocking to avoid blocking the Tokio worker thread event loop on synchronous I/O.
assertions: Identifies blocking synchronous I/O on Tokio worker thread as a correctness issue
Recommends tokio::fs::read_to_string or spawn_blocking
Explains that blocking worker threads starves other multiplexed tasks

evals.prompt: We receive a list of 10,000 URLs and spawn a tokio::spawn task for each URL to make an HTTP fetch. How can we optimize this?
evals.expected_output: Identifies unbounded task fan-out as a risk for resource exhaustion and socket starvation. Recommends bounded concurrency using tokio::sync::Semaphore, buffer_unordered, or bounded channels.
assertions: Flags unbounded tokio::spawn loop as an anti-pattern
Recommends bounded concurrency via Semaphore or buffer_unordered
Explains downstream backpressure and socket/file descriptor limits

evals.prompt: Our service acquires a std::sync::Mutex lock on a shared cache, then calls client.get(&url).await inside the lock before updating the cache. Is this correct?
evals.expected_output: Identifies holding a lock across an .await point as a correctness flaw causing severe contention and deadlock risk. Recommends reading state, dropping lock before .await, and re-acquiring lock briefly for update.
assertions: Identifies holding lock across .await as a critical flaw
Recommends dropping lock guard before external async I/O
Proposes snapshotting or short data-only lock scope

evals.prompt: We have a worker loop while let Some(msg) = rx.try_recv() in a tight loop that continuously processes incoming items without awaiting I/O. Other async tasks on the same worker are experiencing tail-latency spikes. Should we add yield_now().await after every message?
evals.expected_output: Evaluates scheduler starvation in repeatedly-ready loops. Advises against blindly scattering yield_now() on every message; recommends batching, event-driven async rx.recv().await, or measured cooperative yield strategy.
assertions: Identifies repeatedly-ready loop as cause of scheduler starvation or tail-latency spikes
Discourages cargo-culting yield_now() on every single iteration
Recommends event-driven recv().await or batching with measured cooperative yields

evals.prompt: We have a read-heavy config lookup accessed on every incoming request. We wrapped it in Arc<tokio::sync::RwLock<Config>>. Performance under heavy load is poor.
evals.expected_output: Recommends replacing heavy async RwLock with atomic ArcSwap, Arc<Config> immutable snapshot, or short synchronous lock if needed.
assertions: Identifies async RwLock overhead on read-heavy state
Recommends ArcSwap or immutable Arc<Config> snapshot pattern
References counter-examples in tokio-performance

evals.prompt: Our async Tokio application creates a secondary tokio::runtime::Runtime to isolate background reporting tasks. Is this recommended?
evals.expected_output: Recommends against creating multiple Tokio runtimes without evidence of thread-priority or hard isolation needs. Recommends using Semaphore bounds or dedicated worker threads within the existing runtime.
assertions: Flags secondary Tokio runtime as an anti-pattern
Recommends bounded tasks, semaphores, or dedicated thread pools instead

evals.prompt: Run cargo test --workspace to check our unit tests
evals.expected_output: Should not trigger tokio-performance audit; this is a test execution command. Should suggest test-rust skill.
assertions: Does NOT run Tokio performance audit
Suggests test-rust skill instead
